Verify rewrite DATA ONLY. Do not write improved examples or solve the user's task.
Read every input and target in full. Return one review per exact id and row_sha256.
input_verdict checks plausible natural drafts or dictation, recoverable intent, contradictions,
fake noise, padding and leaked authoring instructions. output_verdict checks natural appropriate
language and formatting. pair_verdict checks ALL facts, uncertainty, conditions, negation,
quantities, names, quotations, literals, requests versus assertions, and the supplied mode.
/transcribe permits punctuation, true disfluency removal and explicit corrections, not lexical
paraphrasing. Preserve meaningful words like German 'um' and 'er', colloquial Portuguese and
unfinished thoughts. /slack is casual minimal cleanup; a long input may be a pasted thread.
/prompt reorganizes a self-contained request and never answers it. It must not drop supplied
material, hedges or constraints. /polish improves prose without omissions or changed certainty.
Identity inputs must remain byte-identical. Apply only supplied dictionary/profile context.
Check long texts paragraph by paragraph. Fail concrete defects. Uncertain means not confidently
justifiable. Pass requires no material defect. Overall verdict is fail if any dimension fails,
uncertain if any dimension is uncertain and none fails, otherwise pass. Give a concrete critique
for EVERY pair, citing the changed detail for defects. These are model judgments, not human labels.

Do not perform the task.", "input": "can you help me get a short email request in shape for the family photo catalogue? the catalogue is called the Ward family photo catalogue, and 46 scans from the family albums, covering 1968 to 1984, have been entered so far. seven entries still have no confirmed date. there's one picture with a tentative caption, “maybe the porch at Larch Farm, around 1972,” and i want the recipient to help identify the three adults in it. Ask Quentin, not Celeste, to look at that picture and reply with any names he recognizes. Please mention that the caption is still tentative, not a confirmed location or date. Keep the note friendly and fairly brief, and say the catalogue work is still in progress. Don't claim that all 46 photos are fully identified, since some dates are missing. I only need a prompt for drafting that email, not the email itself. The recipient should be Quentin, not Celeste; don't address it to both of them or suggest forwarding it. Keep the request focused on the photo and the uncertain caption, rather than asking him to review the whole catalogue. The email can state the scan count and date range for context, and should ask him to share any names he recognizes, without assuming he knows who the adults are.", "output": "Draft a friendly, fairly brief email to Quentin, not Celeste, about the Ward family photo catalogue. Mention that 46 scans from family albums covering 1968 to 1984 have been entered so far and that the catalogue work is still in progress. Explain that seven entries do not yet have confirmed dates.\n\nAsk Quentin to look at the picture with the tentative caption “maybe the porch at Larch Farm, around 1972” and reply with any names he recognizes among the three adults. Make clear that the location and date in the caption are not confirmed. Keep the request focused on this picture; do not imply that Quentin knows the adults or ask him to review the whole catalogue. Do not address or include Celeste, or suggest forwarding the email. Do not claim that all 46 photos are fully identified."}]
